title: The object of maps from a finite simplicial set into a simplicial semi-representable object exists
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, let $K$ be a simplicial object of the category $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ of semi-representable objects over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object], and let $S$ be a simplicial set [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] such that $S_n$ is finite and nonempty for every $n\geq0$ and $S$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices. Then there are an object $H$ of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ and morphisms $u_s:H\to K_n$ ($n\geq0$, $s\in S_n$) with $K(\varphi)\circ u_s=u_{S(\varphi)(s)}$ for every $\varphi:[m]\to[n]$ and $s\in S_n$, such that for every object $W$ of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ and every family of morphisms $f_s:W\to K_n$ ($n\geq0$, $s\in S_n$) with $K(\varphi)\circ f_s=f_{S(\varphi)(s)}$ for all $\varphi$ and $s$, there is a unique morphism $g:W\to H$ with $f_s=u_s\circ g$ for all $s$.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\mathrm{SR}(X)$, with its simplicial object $K$ as in the statement, and use [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] for the simplicial operators of $S$. Define a category $\mathcal I_S$: its objects are pairs $(n,s)$ with $s\in S_n$, and a morphism $(m,t)\to(n,s)$ is an order-preserving $\varphi:[m]\to[n]$ with $S(\varphi)(s)=t$. Define $D:\mathcal I_S^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$ by $D(n,s)=K_n$ and by sending this morphism to $K(\varphi):K_n\to K_m$. For an object $W$ of $\mathcal C$, a cone from $W$ to $D$ is exactly a family of morphisms $f_s:W\to K_n$ satisfying $K(\varphi)\circ f_s=f_{S(\varphi)(s)}$ for every $\varphi$ and $s$.

proof.text: Because $S$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices, there is $m_0$ such that every simplex in degree $n>m_0$ is degenerate. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-index-finite-initial] to $\mathcal I_S$: the inclusion of the opposite of its finite full subcategory on degrees at most $2m_0$ into $\mathcal I_S^{\mathrm{op}}$ is initial. The limit-comparison conclusion of that same node (Categories Lemma 002R) therefore identifies the limit of $D$ over $\mathcal I_S^{\mathrm{op}}$ with the limit of its restriction to this finite subcategory.

proof.text: The finite limit in the preceding step exists in $\mathcal C=\mathrm{SR}(X)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-finite-limits], applied to the small etale site of $X$ as in [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object]. Let $H$ be this finite limit. By the comparison clause of [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-index-finite-initial], it also has the universal cone on the full diagram $D$; let $u_s:H\to K_n$ be that cone's component at $(n,s)$, including in degrees above $2m_0$. The cone equations make $(u_s)$ an $S$-family. For any $W$, the cone correspondence in step 1 sends a morphism $g:W\to H$ to the family $(u_s\circ g)_s$, and the universal property of the limit makes this correspondence bijective. Thus $H$ and $(u_s)$ have exactly the universal property asserted in the statement.
